samples.question: This page shows one near-black slab together with coloured rings, frames, blocks and bars as decoration. Only the near-black slab decides the answer; every coloured or grey mark is decoration, never touches the slab, and never counts. The slab was cut from one square block built of small equal square cells, and four white slots have been cut out of it. Each slot is one cell wide, runs along a single straight line of cells, and starts at a border of the block. A slot that reaches the opposite border cuts right through the block there; a slot that stops short leaves a bridge of slab cells at its far end, and the shortest such bridge is one cell wide. Two patches of slab belong to the same piece when you can travel from one to the other over slab only, always stepping between cells that share a whole edge; stepping between two cells that meet at a single corner is not travelling, and no scene requires it. A slot that stops short can still leave its line joined to a neighbouring line only where the two lines still share slab, so slots that stop short on neighbouring lines and start from opposite borders can separate the slab even though neither slot cuts right through. How much dark ink the slab holds, how many slots are cut, how long the slots are, which border each slot starts from, whether the slots run across or down, how large the cells are, where the slab sits on the page, and how many coloured decorations appear never decide the answer. Into how many separate pieces is the slab divided? Answer 1, 2 or 3.
